baslik: The Great Lakes Freighter That Snapped in a November Storm
sonuc: broke in two on Lake Michigan
tetik: a violent storm bending an ageing hull
mekanizma: hull failure amidships in heavy seas, with brittle steel and prior damage suspected
ders: the Coast Guard reviewed hull inspections for ageing lake freighters
yanilgi: The ship wasn't overloaded with cargo. It was sailing light, heading home.
tartisma: Crew letters said the ship was in poor condition. How should crew concerns reach inspectors?
basliklar: Why the Carl D. Bradley Broke in Two
The Freighter That Snapped on Lake Michigan
sahneler: In a November storm, a huge freighter broke in two on Lake Michigan.
It sank in minutes, and almost the entire crew was killed.
The ship was sailing empty, heading home.
Its hull had been damaged in an earlier grounding.
Storm waves flexed the long, ageing ship.
A crack opened amidships and ran across the hull.
Two men survived on a raft through the night.
The Coast Guard reviewed inspections of old lake freighters.

baslik: One Survivor Watched His Ship Break Apart
sonuc: broke in two on Lake Huron
tetik: a storm loading a hull built of brittle steel
mekanizma: hull fracture in cold water, attributed to brittle steel that lost toughness in low temperatures
ders: older lake freighters were reinforced or inspected for brittle steel
yanilgi: The stern kept sailing on its own engines after the bow broke away.
tartisma: Its sister ship had cracks from the same storm. Should a fleet be checked after one ship fails?
basliklar: Why the Daniel J. Morrell Broke Apart
The Brittle Steel of a Great Lakes Freighter
sahneler: In a storm on Lake Huron, a freighter's hull cracked across the deck.
The ship broke in two, and everyone but one sailor died.
The survivor spent a freezing night on a raft.
The stern kept sailing under its own power after the bow fell away.
Investigators blamed the steel.
In cold water, it had become brittle.
Its sister ship had cracked in the same storm.
Older lake freighters were inspected and reinforced afterward.

baslik: A Car Carrier Capsized Leaving Port Because of a Math Error
sonuc: capsized as it left port in Georgia
tetik: a turn on a ship with too little stability
mekanizma: insufficient stability from an incorrect ballast calculation
ders: the operator changed how stability is calculated before departure
yanilgi: No wave or collision tipped it. The ship left port without enough stability to turn.
tartisma: The wreck had to be cut into huge pieces to remove it. How should failures at sea be cleaned up?
basliklar: Why the Golden Ray Capsized
The Stability Error That Rolled a Car Carrier
sahneler: As it left port in Georgia, a giant car carrier suddenly rolled onto its side.
Crew were trapped inside for more than a day before being rescued.
The ship carried thousands of cars.
Its stability calculation was wrong.
Ballast data had been entered incorrectly.
In a normal turn, the ship heeled too far to recover.
The wreck was cut into giant slices to remove it.
The operator changed how stability is checked before departure.

baslik: The Offshore Blowout That Gushed Oil for Nine Months
sonuc: blew out and spilled oil for months
mekanizma: well blowout after loss of mud pressure, with the blowout preventer unable to seal
ders: offshore blowout prevention practices were reviewed internationally
yanilgi: The spill didn't stop when the rig sank. The well kept flowing for months.
tartisma: Relief wells took months to drill. Should they be prepared before drilling starts?
basliklar: Why the Ixtoc I Well Blew Out
The Blowout That Gushed for Nine Months
sahneler: An offshore oil well in the Gulf of Mexico blew out.
Oil and gas exploded upward, and the rig caught fire and sank.
The drilling mud that balanced the well's pressure was lost.
Oil and gas surged up the well.
The blowout preventer couldn't seal it.
The well kept gushing oil for months.
Relief wells finally stopped it.
Blowout prevention practices were reviewed afterward.

baslik: The Well Left Without Its Pressure Caps
sonuc: leaked oil and gas into the Timor Sea for weeks
tetik: a suspended well without its pressure-containing caps
mekanizma: failed cement at the casing shoe plus missing pressure barriers in a suspended well
ders: Australia created a new offshore safety regulator
yanilgi: The well wasn't being drilled at the time. It had been temporarily suspended with barriers missing.
tartisma: The regulator had accepted the operator's own assurances. Who checks the checker?
basliklar: Why the Montara Well Leaked
The Missing Barriers in a Suspended Well
sahneler: An oil well off Australia began leaking uncontrollably.
Within hours, oil and gas spread across the sea, later catching fire.
The well had been temporarily suspended.
Its cement barrier at the bottom had failed.
Pressure-containing caps that should have been installed were not.
The leak continued for more than two months.
The regulator had relied on the operator's assurances.
Australia then created a new offshore safety regulator.

baslik: The Workers Told to Point Radium Brushes With Their Lips
sonuc: were poisoned by the paint they worked with
tetik: shaping radium-paint brushes with their lips
mekanizma: ingestion of radium, which the body deposits in bone like calcium
ders: the cases shaped occupational health and radiation safety standards
yanilgi: Radium wasn't thought dangerous by the workers. Company scientists handled it with protection.
tartisma: The women sued as they were dying. Why does proof of harm fall on the harmed?
basliklar: The Radium Girls and the Poison They Were Told Was Safe
Why Radium Dial Painters Got Sick
sahneler: Young women painted glowing watch dials with radium paint.
Many were later killed by radiation poisoning.
They were taught to shape their brushes with their lips.
Lip, dip, paint.
Each time, they swallowed tiny amounts of radium.
The body stores radium in bone, like calcium.
Their jaws and bones decayed.
Their lawsuits shaped workplace health and radiation safety law.

baslik: The Secret Partial Meltdown Near Los Angeles
tetik: a coolant leak clogging fuel channels
mekanizma: tetralin leaking into the sodium coolant, forming deposits that blocked cooling channels
ders: the site became the focus of a decades-long cleanup
yanilgi: It wasn't widely known for decades. The public learned details long after it happened.
tartisma: Radioactive gas was released intentionally to manage the reactor. How transparent should such decisions be?
basliklar: The Partial Meltdown at Santa Susana
Why the Sodium Reactor Experiment Failed
sahneler: An experimental reactor near Los Angeles suffered a partial meltdown.
Suddenly, fuel elements overheated and were damaged.
It was cooled by liquid sodium.
A second coolant leaked into the sodium.
It formed deposits that blocked cooling channels.
Radioactive gas was vented to the air.
Details became public only years later.
The site has been the focus of a long cleanup.

tetik: an explosion likely involving methane and coal dust
mekanizma: explosion propagated through connected mines by coal dust
ders: the disaster helped lead to the creation of the US Bureau of Mines
yanilgi: The official death toll is likely too low. Many miners' helpers were never recorded.
tartisma: Nobody knew exactly how many were underground. What does that say about worker safety then?
basliklar: Why the Monongah Mines Exploded
America's Deadliest Mining Disaster
sahneler: An explosion tore through two connected coal mines in West Virginia.
It killed at least three hundred sixty two miners.
It remains America's deadliest mining disaster.
The two mines were linked underground.
Coal dust carried the explosion through both.
The true toll is probably higher.
Many helpers underground were never recorded.
It helped lead to the creation of the US Bureau of Mines.

baslik: The Colliery That Exploded Again as Rescuers Went In
sonuc: exploded, then exploded again during the rescue
mekanizma: methane explosions repeated as fires reignited gas
ders: it remains England's worst mining disaster
yanilgi: Many victims were rescuers. Further explosions struck while they searched for survivors.
tartisma: Rescuers went in knowing the danger. How should rescue risk be judged?
basliklar: Why the Oaks Colliery Exploded
The Explosions That Killed the Rescuers
sahneler: A coal mine near Barnsley exploded.
Within hours, three hundred sixty one men and boys were dead.
Methane gas had built up in the workings.
After the first blast, rescuers went down.
Then the mine exploded again.
Many of the dead were rescuers.
The mine had to be sealed.
It remains England's worst mining disaster.

baslik: The Tunnel Ceiling That Fell on Passing Cars
sonuc: had its ceiling collapse onto traffic
tetik: anchor bolts holding ceiling panels pulling out
mekanizma: degradation of adhesive-anchored bolts supporting heavy concrete ceiling panels
ders: Japan ordered inspections of tunnel ceilings and ageing infrastructure
yanilgi: The tunnel itself didn't collapse. Its suspended ceiling panels fell.
tartisma: Inspections relied on looking, not testing the bolts. Is visual inspection enough?
basliklar: Why the Sasago Tunnel Ceiling Collapsed
The Anchor Bolts That Let Go
sahneler: Concrete ceiling panels fell inside a Japanese expressway tunnel.
They crushed passing vehicles, and nine people were killed.
The tunnel itself stayed intact.
The heavy panels hung from anchor bolts glued into the rock.
Over decades, the adhesive degraded.
Bolts pulled out, and a long stretch of panels came down.
Inspections had been mostly visual.
Japan then ordered checks of tunnels and ageing infrastructure.

baslik: Two Trucks Collided Inside a 17-Kilometre Tunnel
sonuc: filled with fire and smoke after a truck collision
tetik: two trucks colliding head-on inside the tunnel
mekanizma: vehicle fire in a long bidirectional tunnel producing smoke faster than people could escape
ders: Switzerland introduced truck spacing rules for the tunnel
yanilgi: Most victims weren't burned. Smoke overtook them as they tried to escape.
tartisma: Two-way traffic shares one tube. Should every long tunnel have two?
basliklar: Why the Gotthard Tunnel Fire Was So Deadly
The Truck Collision Deep Inside the Alps
sahneler: Two trucks collided head-on deep inside the Gotthard road tunnel.
Fire and smoke spread through the tunnel, and eleven people died.
The tunnel carries traffic both ways in one tube.
The crash set the trucks on fire.
Thick smoke spread faster than people could walk out.
Heat caused part of the ceiling to collapse.
Rescue teams struggled to reach the fire.
Switzerland introduced spacing rules for trucks in the tunnel.

baslik: The San Francisco Skyscraper That Is Sinking and Tilting
sonuc: sank and tilted more than expected
tetik: foundation piles that stop short of bedrock
mekanizma: settlement of a heavy concrete tower on friction piles in compressible soil, worsened by nearby dewatering
ders: a retrofit added new piles down to bedrock on one side
yanilgi: The tower isn't about to fall. But it settled and tilted far beyond what was predicted.
tartisma: The foundation met approvals at the time. Who pays when a building sinks?
basliklar: Why San Francisco's Millennium Tower Is Sinking
The Skyscraper That Didn't Reach Bedrock
soru: Who pays when a tower sinks?
sahneler: A luxury skyscraper in San Francisco began sinking and tilting.
Within years, it had settled far more than engineers predicted.
The tower is made of heavy concrete.
Its piles stop in soil instead of reaching bedrock.
The soft layers below compressed under the weight.
Nearby construction also drew water from the ground.
A retrofit added new piles down to bedrock.
The fix itself caused more settlement before it was adjusted.
